home.title: Crossing over from noise and disconnection to what is real right where we live.
home.intro: Crossover Stockton is an organization of awareness and practical local action. We drop blame, use AI and public records as a clear mirror to see where our community’s systems fall short, and focus our hands where real fruit can grow.

home.imageCaption: STOCKTON, CALIFORNIA · SEE CLEARLY. ACT LOCALLY.

priorities.name: Upstream Spay/Neuter Surgical & Scheduling Bottleneck
priorities.summary: Multi-week surgical waitlists and scheduling friction prevent willing low-income pet families from sterilizing dogs before accidental litters occur.

priorities.name: Appointment-Only Shelter Intake Wall & Field Dispatch Latency
priorities.summary: Overcrowded kennels force appointment-only stray intake, leaving finders without immediate drop-off options and stretching field trucks thin.

priorities.name: Willing-Helper & Volunteer Onboarding Stall (Doggie Day Out / Foster)
priorities.summary: Residents applying to walk shelter dogs or temporarily foster found strays face unanswered email queues due to overwhelmed administrative bandwidth.

carePaths.name: A lost family dog
carePaths.need: A safe scan and a reliable lost-pet report.
carePaths.next: Check identification and connect the dog with its family when possible.

carePaths.name: An injured dog alone
carePaths.need: A safe report, urgent assessment, and transport to care.
carePaths.next: Confirm who can respond and where the dog can recover.

carePaths.name: A dog with a person in crisis
carePaths.need: Support for the person and dog together.
carePaths.next: Ask about pet-accessible services before assuming the dog needs intake.

doing.title: What we're doing
doing.intro: Our work follows a simple loop: identify a need, make the next step clear, and help locally. These are the actions we have documented and the work still ahead, with the source record attached to each item.

steps.label: NOTICE
steps.text: Identify a real need and listen to people close to it.

steps.label: CONNECT
steps.text: Clarify the next handoff and who can help.

steps.label: ACT
steps.text: Follow through with practical local support.

ai.intro: We use AI as a clear mirror, not an idol. It can help us see where care stalls and remove practical friction for everyday people. Local partners still confirm the facts, make decisions, and provide the care.

ideas.title: Spay/neuter & clinic navigator
ideas.friction: A person can find a clinic name yet still miss the right service, eligibility rule, appointment step, or way to get there.
ideas.role: A plain-English guide could ask about location, dog size and age, and urgency, then show checked care options and what to ask when booking. Live openings would appear only if a provider confirms them.

ideas.title: Found-dog & temporary foster guide
ideas.friction: A finder may not know where to request a microchip scan, report a found pet, or ask about a temporary foster route when shelter drop-off requires a call.
ideas.role: A guided path could separate urgent injury from a likely lost pet, link to the City's lost-and-found guidance, and show the next contact. Foster availability would require a current answer from the shelter or partner.

ideas.title: Outreach signal organizer
ideas.friction: Reports of a dog in need can be scattered or duplicated, leaving outreach partners unsure whether they describe one dog or several.
ideas.role: AI could group public reports for human review and help a local partner decide whom to contact. A suggested match would remain a lead, not a verified sighting or dispatch decision.

ideas.title: Public data watcher
ideas.friction: Shelter figures can change while older numbers remain in articles and community discussions.
ideas.role: A watcher could flag changes in public releases, keep the source and date attached, and prompt a person to check whether species, period, and service area still match before updating a claim.

aside.title: Why an unrestricted dog drop-off space is not our plan
aside.intro: An open place for every found dog sounds welcoming. It needs more than a gate and a yard to be safe or sustainable.

points.title: Prevent the next intake
points.text: Without reachable spay and neuter care, new litters can keep arriving faster than a temporary space can help them.

points.title: Protect dogs and people
points.text: Injured, contagious, and fearful dogs need assessment, separation when appropriate, trained handling, and a real route onward.

aside.conclusion: We are focusing on care access, reunion, and confirmed temporary placements that partners can actually support.
